title: Trade & Supply Chain
headline_read: Trade frictions are building — supply chains or import costs bear watching.

indicators.title: Global Supply Chain Pressure Index
indicators.context: The NY Fed's gauge of global supply-chain strain — shipping costs, delivery times, and backlogs rolled into one index, measured in standard deviations from normal. The COVID logjam peaked near 4.5σ; negative means looser than normal.
indicators.read: Supply-chain pressure is 1.2σ above normal — tighter than usual.

indicators.title: Import Prices · year-over-year
indicators.context: How fast the prices of everything the U.S. imports are rising versus a year ago. Tariffs, a weaker dollar, and supply shocks all show up here first — before they reach store shelves.
indicators.read: Import costs are rising 6.7% a year — climbing.

indicators.title: U.S. Trade Deficit · goods & services
indicators.context: How much more the U.S. imports than it exports, in billions per month. The U.S. has run a deficit every year since 1976 — what matters is whether it is widening or narrowing, and why.
indicators.read: The U.S. trade deficit is $55.9B a month, narrower than a year ago.
indicators.no_severity_reason: The U.S. has run a trade deficit every year since 1976 — the level isn't good or bad on its own; what matters is the trend shown here.

indicators.title: China Exports · year-over-year
indicators.context: The growth of China's exports versus a year ago — the single best pulse on global goods demand, since China ships roughly a seventh of the world's exports.
indicators.read: China's export trade is rising 13.8% a year.
indicators.no_severity_reason: Shown for context — a noisy global-demand pulse the lens's scored indicators read more cleanly.
